result.title: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits
result.summary: Heavy-tailed bandit learners without moment parameters face an obstruction: the rewards that carry an arm's mean can stay unseen. We address the remaining part of a COLT open problem by characterizing the optimal-arm laws that permit adaptation to unknown moments at constant-factor cost. The condition, variance-core visibility, is one-sided and translation-invariant: the mean hidden in any rare event is at most a constant multiple of the standard error of the rewards that remain. A quantile-trimmed UCB index that knows the visibility constants attains the central-moment benchmark on this class, and no single strategy adapts across all visibility levels. The same index achieves logarithmic expected regret on every instance with a visible optimal arm and finite-mean rewards. On an explicit family with no higher moment, gap $Δ$ and constant $A$, its logarithmic coefficient and the information lower bound are of order $Δ^{-1}e^{A/Δ}$, exponential in the inverse gap within one visibility class.

AI.brief_summary: 研究重尾 bandit 在矩参数未知时的自适应：提出「方差核心可见性」这一单侧、平移不变条件，给出分位数截尾 UCB 索引，刻画可常数因子达到中心矩基准的最优臂分布类，并说明不存在跨可见性层统一的单一策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「承载均值的证据可能藏在稀有事件中」与按可见性分层的不可适应结果，可能为 LVR 中稀有但关键的视觉证据获取、LOOK/STOP 决策与信息下界评价提供问题表述线索，可供核查。
